site.name: Stocka
site.description: A clear inventory for your items: what they are, where they are and who owns them. No spreadsheets, no chaos.

hero.sub: Stocka is a clear inventory for your items: what they are, where they're located, who really owns them and all their information. No spreadsheets, no chaos.

features.title: Everything you need to take control of your inventory.
features.sub: Built for teams that need to know what they have and where, without setting up an entire ERP.

item.title: Complete record per item
item.body: Name, description, serial number, photos and documents. All the information in one place.

location.title: Physical location
location.body: Room, shelf, drawer… Define the hierarchy that fits best and find any item instantly.

owner.title: Real owner
owner.body: Track who actually owns each item, not just who keeps it. Ideal for shared assets.

category.title: Types and categories
category.body: Group by item type and add custom fields to match each kind. No rigid forms.

label.title: Codes and labels
label.body: Generate and print labels with QR or barcode. Scan with your phone to view the record instantly.

history.title: History and audit
history.body: Every move, transfer or change of owner is recorded with date and responsible party.

how.title: Start tracking your inventory in 10 minutes.
how.sub: Import your list, invite your team and start logging items. Just like that.

create.title: Create your items
create.body: Upload a CSV or add them by hand. Define the types, locations and owners that match your case.

invite.title: Invite your team
invite.body: Add your teammates with roles and permissions. Each person sees and edits what is theirs.

maintain.title: Keep the record alive
maintain.body: Transfers, owner changes and updates from mobile or desktop. Everything is audited.

testimonial.label: Testimonial
testimonial.quote: “We had assets scattered across offices and nobody knew whose was whose. With Stocka we find any item in seconds and we always know who it belongs to.”
testimonial.author: Laura Méndez

cta.label: Call to action
cta.title: Bring order to your inventory today.
cta.sub: Start free, no card needed. Create your first item in a couple of minutes and see if it fits.

footer.tagline: Simple, honest inventory for teams who want to know what they have, where it is and whose it is.

connection_help.relay: A relay sits on a Raspberry Pi GPIO or on a channel (0–15) of an MCP23017 expander, never both.
connection_help.sensor: A digital sensor sits on a Raspberry Pi GPIO (recommended for the emergency stop and limit switches) or on a channel (0–15) of an MCP23017 expander, never both. A sensor that measures (distance, temperature…) is wired as its model requires.
connection_help.motor: The two H-bridge outputs (IN1/IN2) go on two Raspberry Pi GPIOs or on two channels of the same MCP23017 expander, never mixed.
connection_help.sensor_measured: Reads a value (distance, temperature…) with the chosen model and becomes active when the value crosses the threshold. It works like a digital one: a motor limit switch or “When active”.

connection_no_expanders.relay: No expanders in the organization: the relay goes on a GPIO. Create a “Relay expander” port for more outputs.
connection_no_expanders.sensor: No expanders in the organization: the sensor goes on a GPIO.
connection_no_expanders.motor: No expanders in the organization: the motor goes on two GPIOs.
connection_no_expanders.sensor_measured: Reads a value with the chosen model and becomes active when it crosses the threshold.

form.motor_outputs_distinct: The two motor outputs (forward and reverse) must be different.
form.trig_echo_distinct: TRIG and ECHO must be on different GPIOs.

config_help.last: Between 0 and the strip LED count minus 1.
config_help.strip: Name of a LED strip port.
config_help.pinReverse: H-bridge output IN2; different from the forward one.
config_help.channelReverse: Expander channel for IN2; different from the forward one.
config_help.switchDelayMs: Time with both outputs off when changing direction. 50 ms is enough with an H-bridge; with mechanical relays, 300 ms or more.
config_help.maxTimeForward: Hard cut: the motor never turns forward longer than this in one go, no matter what. The turning time is the clip length.
config_help.maxTimeReverse: Hard cut for the reverse direction.
config_help.limitForward: Sensor port that stops the motor when it fires while turning forward; if it is already active, the motor does not start.
config_help.limitReverse: Sensor port that stops the motor when it fires while turning in reverse.
config_help.lockOnTimeout: If a direction with a limit switch ends by its maximum time, besides the alert the motor stays locked until someone unlocks it on the Raspberry Pi.
config_help.pull: Internal resistor of the input; on an expander, only up or none.
config_help.debounceMs: A change only counts if it holds for this long.
config_help.onActive: What the player does with the show when the sensor becomes active.
config_help.activeLow: The output switches on at low level (opto-isolated relay boards).
config_help.expander: Expander port the relay hangs from.
config_help.address: First DMX channel of the fixture (DMX Address menu); it takes 15 channels and cannot overlap another head.

gpio_expander.address: Unique per bus. With an expander, GPIO 2 and 3 (I2C) are reserved.
gpio_expander.activeLow: Polarity of the whole relay board wired to the expander.

config_help.model: What it measures and how it is wired (see the note under the title).
config_help.quantity: This model measures more than one: choose which one the threshold watches.
config_help.pinTrig: 3.3 V output to the module’s TRIG.
config_help.pinEcho: ECHO input, through a voltage divider if the module runs at 5 V.
config_help.deviceId: Optional: 28- and 12 hex digits (under /sys/bus/w1/devices). Without it, the first sensor on the bus.
config_help.threshold: Within the range the model measures.
config_help.activeWhen: Below: active when the value reaches the threshold or goes under it (e.g. the angel closer than 20 cm). Above: when it exceeds it.
config_help.hysteresis: Margin to release, so it does not flicker right at the threshold.
config_help.pollMs: How often the value is read.

sensor.expander: Expander port that owns the input channel.
sensor.activeLow: Active when the input is low (contact to ground with pull-up). Untick it for sensors that drive the line high.
sensor.address: One of the addresses the model accepts, in decimal (0x29 = 41, 0x76 = 118, 0x77 = 119). Unique per bus with the expanders; with any I2C device, GPIO 2 and 3 are reserved.

motor.activeLow: Both outputs switch on at low level.

moving_head.profile: Fixture model: channels, pan/tilt/zoom ranges and DMX conversion.

onActive.none: Only motors use it, as a limit switch.
onActive.play: Start button of the nativity scene: a short press starts a run; held for 10 s it opens the Raspberry Pi’s own Wi-Fi and for 30 s it puts everything in safe mode.
onActive.stop_show: Stops the current run, leaves the outputs safe and raises an alert.
onActive.panic: Puts everything in safe mode, keeps the player safe until someone re-enables it and raises an alert. It cannot be cut.
